internal_decisions: Absolute-zero check compares the Celsius value rounded to 9 decimals, to absorb float error (e.g. -459.67 F)
Conversion goes through Celsius; only the final result is rounded
Regex with fullmatch; accepts optional sign, decimals like '.5' and '5.', surrounding whitespace; ASCII only.

plan: Contracts/integration: parse→convert flow, absolute-zero boundaries per unit, unknown units on either side. Pass.
Edge cases: malformed parse inputs (exponent, comma, nan, underscore, Unicode digits, double sign), accepted forms. Pass.
Edge cases that fail: NaN/inf in convert (D1, D2), quadratic parse time (D3). These tests stay red on purpose (medium/low).
Regression, non-functional (beyond parse performance): discarded, no pre-existing behaviour at risk.

defects.repro: convert(float('nan'),'C','F') returns nan instead of raising, because the comparison with absolute zero is False for NaN.
defects.fix: Reject non-finite input with math.isfinite(value) and raise ValueError.
defects.if_skipped: NaN passes through as a valid temperature and corrupts downstream data.

defects.repro: convert(float('inf'),'C','F') returns inf instead of raising.
defects.if_skipped: Infinite temperatures are accepted as valid.

defects.repro: parse('1'*20000+'XC') raises ValueError only after seconds of CPU (about 6s with all tests in the run; 100000 digits took over 2 minutes). The regex `\d+\.?\d*` backtracks quadratically on a long digit string with a bad suffix.
defects.fix: Use an unambiguous pattern such as `\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+`, or reject text longer than a sane limit before matching.
defects.if_skipped: Untrusted text of a few KB can tie up a CPU, a denial of service for any service that calls parse.

gaps: parse('1C\n') is accepted (trailing whitespace). The spec says 'optional spaces', so this is ambiguous and I did not report it as a defect.
Non-str input to parse (e.g. None) raises TypeError. The contract is typed str, so I did not test it.
I could not run ad-hoc python3 -c commands (the sandbox required approval), so every probe went into the test file.

advisory.problem: The AC-002 rounding check for 20.555 C to K allows a delta of 0.011, so 293.70 and 293.71 both pass. The test would not catch a floor or truncate instead of round, but it does enforce at most 2 decimals.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that truncates to 2 decimals returns 293.7 and passes. The exact-value tests for 100 F to 37.78 and 0 K to -273.15 still catch most wrong rounding.

advisory.problem: The AC-005 tests only assert ValueError and don't check the message. The brief only asks for ValueError, so this is acceptable. There is no test for a negative or decimal number without a unit, or for a space between number and unit with an invalid unit.
advisory.evidence: No trivial stub passes. A constant return fails AC-004, and raising ValueError for everything fails AC-001, AC-002 and AC-004.
